Subject: Sudden spike in 504s this morning — urgent

Diego —

We're seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and intermittent 504s from your hosted endpoint (model: redwood/large-2028-q). It started ~08:40 PT and corresponds with a batch-growth event on our side (we always multiplex brief requests). Throughput briefly dropped and a subset of endpoints returned repeated 504s and elevated p99.

Attached are a short trace dump and a CSV of request IDs (cdm-extract-20290609.csv). This is impacting a live feature — customers are seeing degraded response times. Can you confirm you can repro or provide a mitigation plan? We're on a tight renewal cadence and need a quick action.

Subject: Re: Sudden spike in 504s this morning — urgent

Theo — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the artifacts. I'm triaging now. Initial sightlines: a burst of small, highly concurrent requests triggered an automatic batching ramp on a subset of the fleet. That, combined with recent KV cache config changes for short TTLs, looks like it caused cache entries to thrash and a head-of-line (HOL) blocking condition on several hot shards.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- I'll kick a targeted configuration rollback for the short-TTL policy on the nodes serving your tenant (5–10 min window).
- Ops (Jonas) will temporarily restrict the maximum batch size for your route to reduce per-request queuing.
- We'll push a hotfix to skip batch-aggregation when observed batch growth exceeds expected envelope (mitigation only) and keep you posted.

Can you confirm whether Solaris ramped any new traffic patterns or a new client release around 08:30–08:45 PT? That will help root cause.

I'll update in ~15–20 mins.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 Jun 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in 504s this morning — urgent

Quick update from ops: we observed 504 clusters pinned to three host groups. Median queue depth spiked where the batch assembler tried to grow batch sizes aggressively (auto-batching heuristic reacted to concurrency), which amplified KV cache miss amplification. Result: small hot keys kept getting evicted and then re-fetched, producing repeated kV reads and a HOL stall while the batch waited for remaining tokens.

Actions taken (10:00–10:20 PT):
- Rolled back short-TTL cache policy for Solaris tenancy (rollforward halted).
- Temporarily capped batch size from 64 -> 24 for the route (reduces queueing; minor throughput loss).
- Applied a locality pin (bind hot keys to fewer partitions) to reduce cross-shard pull.

Preliminary result: p99 improved from 2.3s -> 1.0s on sampled traffic; 504s down 85% on the affected hosts. Still seeing intermittent tail spikes during sustained concurrent bursts.

Please include whether Sales/CS need an exec note for Solaris. I think we should loop in Marissa for a longer-term runtime fix.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Ops

Subject: Re: Sudden spike in 504s this morning — urgent

Thx team. Technical summary and suggested roadmap:

Root cause hypothesis:
- Aggressive auto-batching increase exposed a pathological interaction with a recent KV eviction policy (short TTLs + small cache size for per-tenant partitions). Hot key churn caused repeated cache misses and synchronous fetches, which then blocked batch completion (HOL).

Short-term (next 24 hrs):
1) Keep the batch cap in place and TTL rollback (ops actioned).
2) Temporarily enable per-tenant prefix caching (increase local cache allocation for Solaris) to dampen misses.
3) Add a protective guard to the batch assembler: if a batch waits > 120ms for missing members, flush partial batch instead of waiting for full assembly (avoid HOL lock).

Medium-term (2–4 weeks):
- Re-evaluate default eviction policy; introduce an adaptive TTL per-tenant that considers request size distribution.
- Add telemetry for batch-assembly latencies and per-key eviction churn.
- Consider bucketized hot-key reservations for high-QPS tenants (reservation trades a bit of memory for stability).

Business note: Rishi — Solaris is on an upcoming renewal and raised procurement-level visibility (cc included). Recommend an exec sync to reassure and to propose a short service credit if we miss SLA in the 72-hr window.

I'll draft a post-mortem template after stabilization.

— Marissa Cole
Head of Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference

Theo — quick status and next steps (TL;DR: mitigations in place; working on durable fixes).

What we did so far:
- Rolled back the short-TTL KV policy for your tenant and increased local cache allocation (immediate effect on miss amplification).
- Limited batch size on your route to reduce queueing and prevent HOL waiting.
- Applied a temporary guard to flush partial batches that exceed 120ms wait; this reduces head-of-line stalls while we tune.

Observed impact:
- 504s down ~90% on sampled fleets; p99 improved substantially. Residual spikes remain only under extreme sustained concurrency (we have mitigations in staging).

Planned next steps:
1) Engineering (Marissa) will work a 2-week patch to introduce adaptive eviction/TTL and batch-assembly heuristics.
2) Ops (Jonas) to run a focused load test with Solaris traffic profile to validate.
3) CS (Rishi) to coordinate a 2PM PT exec sync tomorrow to walk Solaris through the mitigation and roadmap; recommend offering a goodwill service credit if SLA breach is verified.

Can Solaris share whether any client-side retries or fanout changed around 08:30–08:45 PT? That will help finalize the post-mortem.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this feels bad on a live feature. We'll follow up with a technical write-up and a timeline for the code fix.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
